newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria says CA merger in national interest.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria says CA merger in national interest.

text.p: Bank Austria, responding to European Commission approval of its takeover of Creditanstalt, said on Wednesday the new bank would represent national interests but kept silent on strategy.

"The teaming up of Bank Austria and Creditanstalt is a purely Austrian solution (to the privatisation of Creditanstalt) that will have a positive effect on the domestic banking sector and the entire Austrian economy," Bank Austria said in a statement.

"Austria's biggest banking group will set the pace for Austria's banking sector on the road to a new Europe. Because of its market position and development potential it will effectively represent Austrian interests - at home and abroad."
The European Commission gave the green light to the 17.2 billion schillings ($1.4 billion) merger of Austria's first and second banks on Tuesday but linked its approval to several conditions.

The new bank, with total assets of more than 1,300 billion schillings, must sell its stake in savings bank GiroCredit, and reduce its interest in export financing agent Kontrollbank and municipal financing body Investkredit.
The Commission also required Bank Austria to reduce its dominant position in domestic construction by selling Creditanstalt's shares in market leader Universale UNBV.VI or its own stake in Stuag.
Bank Austria made no comment on the conditions. It has already agreed to the sale of a 56 percent stake in GiroCredit to savings bank Die Erste, reportedly for 8.2 billion schillings.
Creditanstalt also declined comment until Bank Austria made clear its future strategy, probably not before next week. Bank Austria's board will hold a news conference on March 17.
"The primary goal of the new banking group is to achieve the maximum in its offer of services and products as well as a high degree of efficiency," the statement said, without expanding.
Bank Austria reiterated its commitment to reduce the combined bank's workforce through natural wastage. It also promised continuity to the customers of both banks. ($ = 12.03 Austrian Schillings)
